Wait, but the orange moved to (16, 38), which is different from the previous path positions (17, 21), (17, 17). This is a new path!
Let me track the orange's position:
- Before: orange at (17, 30), white at (21, 8)
- After: orange at (16, 38), white at (17, 30)
The orange moved from (17, 30) to (16, 38). This is a different direction than before. Previously, the orange moved from (17, 30) to (17, 21) to (17, 17).
So the orange's path depends on where the white diamond is. When the white was at (18, 57), the orange moved towards (17, 21). When the white was at (21, 8), the orange moved towards (16, 38).
Wait, that doesn't make sense. Let me re-examine.
Actually, looking at the previous sequence:
1. White at (18, 57), orange at (17, 30) -> click orange -> orange at (17, 21), white at (17, 30)
2. White at (17, 30), orange at (17, 21) -> click orange -> orange at (17, 17), white at (17, 21)
3. White at (17, 21), orange at (17, 17) -> click orange -> white disappears, orange at (17, 17)
But now:
1. White at (21, 8), orange at (17, 30) -> click orange -> orange at (16, 38), white at (17, 30)
The orange moved to a different position because the white was at a different position. So the orange's movement depends on the white's position.
Hmm, but the orange at (16, 38) is near the light gray trail at (17, 47). Let me check the adjacency.
Actually, let me look at the light gray trail objects:
- w(6) at (15, 33)
- w(10) at (17, 47)
These are different from the previous trail objects:
- w(11) at (17, 38)
- w(6) at (18, 24)
- w(11) at (18, 49)
- w(5) at (19, 19)
- w(6) at (20, 13)
The trail objects changed! This suggests the path changed based on the white's position.
So the mechanic is:
1. The white diamond determines the path
2. Clicking on the orange moves it along the path determined by the white's position
3. The white follows the orange
Let me continue clicking on the orange to see where it goes.
